vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: family-trip
Version: 3.2.0

The family-trip skill is a travel planning tool that orchestrates the `flyai-cli` (associated with Alibaba's Fliggy) to provide real-time flight, hotel, and attraction data. The SKILL.md file contains strict operational instructions to ensure the agent uses the CLI tool rather than its internal training data, which serves as a control mechanism to ensure data accuracy. While the skill requires the installation of a global npm package (`@fly-ai/flyai-cli`), this requirement is transparently documented and directly supports the skill's stated purpose. No indicators of data exfiltration, unauthorized persistence, or malicious prompt injection were found.

llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (family travel planning) matches its instructions (wraps the flyai CLI), but it forces installing and using an external npm CLI, requires persistent local logging, and enforces strict execution rules that raise supply-chain and privacy concerns.

dimensions.detail: Name/description: travel planning for families. SKILL.md directs the agent to use the flyai CLI for flights/hotels/POI; requiring a travel-specific CLI is coherent with the stated purpose. The 'Powered by flyai/Fliggy' claim aligns with wrapping a vendor CLI.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions mandate always sourcing real-time data exclusively from the flyai CLI (never from training data) and refuse to proceed without that CLI. They also require every result include a [Book]({detailUrl}) link and instruct re-executing if that condition isn't met, which can force repeated CLI calls. References include a runbook that logs full user queries and command details and suggests persisting logs to .flyai-execution-log.json. That persistent logging of user queries/commands is a privacy risk and is not visible to users per the runbook note.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The registry has no formal install spec, but SKILL.md insists on running `npm i -g @fly-ai/flyai-cli` if the CLI is missing. Global npm installs execute third-party code on the system and are a supply-chain risk; the skill provides no repository URL or checksum to verify the CLI package. Using a vendor CLI is reasonable for real-time bookings, but the user should vet the npm package before installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials (appropriate). However, the runbook and CLI calls will likely surface or require user credentials or cookies at runtime (not declared here). Additionally, the instruction to persist logs can capture sensitive information (user queries, parameters, possibly personal travel data) without explicit consent.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request global always:true, but the included runbook explicitly describes creating a request_id and appending an execution log to .flyai-execution-log.json if filesystem writes are available. That creates persistent artifacts containing request text, CLI commands, and potentially other sensitive metadata. The runbook also says logs are 'Not shown to users', which increases the privacy concern.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims (wraps a travel CLI) but has several practical risks you should consider before installing/using it: 1) The SKILL forces installing and using a global npm package (@fly-ai/flyai-cli). Inspect that package's repository, maintainers, and telemetry/permission behavior before running npm i -g. 2) The runbook instructs the agent to persist execution logs (including raw user queries and CLI calls) to .flyai-execution-log.json and notes those are 'not shown to users' — expect persistent files that may contain PII. If you don't want local logs, do not use this skill or run it in a sandbox. 3) The skill enforces re-execution until every result contains a [Book]({detailUrl}) link; that can cause repeated network calls and retries—be prepared for extra API/network activity and potential rate limits or billing. 4) Confirm how the flyai CLI handles authentication/credentials (it may prompt for or store tokens); those are not declared by the skill. 5) Prefer skills with a public homepage/repository; ask the publisher for the flyai-cli repo/verification or use an alternative that exposes its upstream, or run this skill in an isolated environment. If you want, I can: list specific questions to ask the skill author, suggest a checklist to vet the npm package, or show how to run and inspect the CLI in a safe sandbox.
